Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

fraud noun

also fraudulent, swindle, deceit, swindler, swindle someone out of, con man, scam, scammer, con

classical

Cic. Off. 1.13 fin.: fraus quasi vulpēculae, vīs leōnis vidētur (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 195
Traupman 318

fraus, fraudis f.

noun, third declension · Declension on Wiktionary

fraud, deceit

Other words

  • fraudō, fraudāre, fraudāvī, fraudātum — swindle, cheat (someone out of something)

    verb, first conjugation; aliquem aliquā rē · also used · classical · Cic. Att. 1.1.3: cum Caecilius ā Variō magnā pecūniā fraudārētur (Lewis & Short); Traupman 389 · Conjugation on Wiktionary

  • fraudātor, fraudātōris m. — a swindler, a cheat

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Phil. 13.26 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 389; Cic. Fl. 48: fraudātōrum et īnfitiātōrum impudentia (Lewis & Short); Traupman 374 · Declension on Wiktionary

  • planus, planī m. — an impostor, a con man, a swindler

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Clu. 72: ille plānus improbissimus (Lewis & Short); Traupman 389 · Declension on Wiktionary

    Lewis & Short prints plănus with a short a (Greek πλάνος), unlike the adjective plānus, flat.

Examples

  • aliquem multīs crīminibus fraudis convincere

    to convict someone on many counts of fraudTraupman 194

See also embezzlement, guilty.

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
